Unsupported assertion, administrative convenience alone or an inclusive label does not satisfy that burden. Racial hierarchy, stereotypes, hostility, political favoritism and racial allocation for its own sake are impermissible objectives.

Supported correction of discrimination and exclusion, prevention of their recurrence and supported efforts to overcome continuing barriers to meaningful market participation are permissible objectives. An adjudicated violation by every implementing office, proof that each beneficiary personally suffered discrimination and a prior judgment against each private contractor are not universal prerequisites. The government must identify the relevant barrier or condition and explain why the racial measure substantially addresses it; a corrective purpose alone does not establish validity. Metro Broadcasting's lower tier for benign federal racial classifications is overruled, and Croson's categorical strict-scrutiny formulation is displaced while its demand for relevant evidence is retained. The standard governs a State university's admissions classifications, local contracting preferences and municipal promotion preferences alike; general inequality, numerical imbalance and good intentions alone do not supply the justification.

In K–12 public schooling, supported educational benefits from meaningful integration and avoidance of serious racial isolation may constitute an important lawful objective. An existing desegregation decree is not a prerequisite to that objective, and its absence proves neither a remedial duty nor invalidity. Demographic percentages, annual classifications or a beneficial label do not establish the educational condition, substantial fit or justification of individual burdens; no duty to adopt preferences or presumption validating numerical targets follows.

Intentional selection for police investigation by race is a racial classification even when the identifying feature came from a victim and officials lack racial hostility. A supported description can justify appropriately fitted investigation, but neither its source nor consensual questioning removes the selection from this standard. Courts examine the actual criteria, coverage and burdens; individual injury, responsibility, immunity and relief require their own predicates. A description's age, sex, injury, place and time features may bear on fit, without becoming mandatory factors in every investigation.

**Authority by component:**

- Objective, evidence-supported relationship, coverage, burdens and alternatives; permissible and impermissible objectives; absence of universal prerequisites; application to federal, state and local government; overruling of Metro's lower federal tier and displacement of Croson's categorical formulation: Adarand Constructors, Inc. v. Peña — The common substantial-justification standard, 1995-06-12; Chief Justice Stone-Zsela's opinion of the Court, joined in full by Stevens, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer (five). O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas concur in the judgment on strict-scrutiny grounds and do not join the standard.
- State university admissions classifications: Hopwood v. Texas — I. The established unequal admissions process, 1996-11-25; O'Connor, all nine.
- Local contracting classifications and the alternatives inquiry applied to responsive race-neutral measures: Engineering Contractors Association of South Florida v. Metropolitan Dade County — The local racial classifications are subject to Adarand's common standard and The BBE and HBE programs fail the governing standard's alternatives requirement, 1998-09-21; O'Connor for the Court, Parts II and III with all eight Associates.
- Municipal promotion preferences and the distinct sex standard: City of Dallas v. Dallas Fire Fighters Association — Local racial and sex classifications retain distinct constitutional standards, 1999-06-18; Kennedy's Part I, all nine.

- Eisenberg v. Montgomery County Public Schools; Fourth Circuit No. 98-2503, 197 F.3d 123; no Supreme Court docket supplied. — Canonical Decision Record, Holdings, I. The actual transfer restriction must satisfy the common standard; II. Supported educational benefits of K–12 integration may qualify, 2000-05-30; Stone-Zsela Part I with Stevens, O'Connor, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer (seven); Part II with Stevens, O'Connor, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer (six), Kennedy reserving that affirmative objective.

- Canonical Decision Record `brown-v-city-of-oneonta_merits_2001-11-13.md`, Public Projection / Holdings / Deliberate racial selection requires justification; Remand rule, 2001-11-13; O'Connor's unanimous opinion.

**Present operation effective:** Brown v. City of Oneonta, November 13, 2001, extends the classification trigger to purposeful investigative selection; the earlier substantive standard and educational component retain their stated dates.

**Exceptions and limits:** The standard is constitutional permission within lawful governmental authority, not a constitutional command to adopt preferences or a freestanding power to regulate every private inequality, and it supplies no universal exemption for corrective measures. Congress may justify a national remedial category through authority and evidence unavailable to a municipality's independently designed measure; an agency need not reproduce Congress's entire evidentiary case for each project but must remain within its delegation and justify materially different or unsupported implementation. No single disparity ratio, regression method, commissioned study, least-restrictive-means formula, mandatory consultation procedure or permanent judicial monitoring system is constitutionalized. Sex-equality doctrine and other source-specific protections are not replaced; Shaw's design-only districting rule and the Voting Rights Act's statutory elements are untouched.

**Related current rules:** Race-conscious public-university admissions and individual relief; Race-conscious local public-contracting preferences; Sex-conscious public-contracting preferences; Territorial racial design and independently cognizable injury.

**Holdings navigation:** Adarand Constructors, Inc. v. Peña (1995-06-12) — Civil Rights / Governmental racial classifications (The common substantial-justification standard; Vacatur and bounded remand under the common standard); Federal Courts / Equal-competition standing and continuing injury (Equal competitive opportunity and prospective standing). Hopwood v. Texas (1996-11-25) — The established unequal admissions process. Engineering Contractors Association of South Florida v. Metropolitan Dade County (1998-09-21) — The local racial classifications are subject to Adarand's common standard; The BBE and HBE programs fail the governing standard's alternatives requirement. City of Dallas v. Dallas Fire Fighters Association (1999-06-18) — Local racial and sex classifications retain distinct constitutional standards.

## Standards and Tests selection: Tribal civil authority over defined nonmember land-use and enforcement settings

### Tribal civil authority over defined nonmember land-use and enforcement settings

**Governing question:** Tribal civil authority over ordinary public-highway users, nonmember fee-land guest transactions and state process investigating off-reservation offenses on retained trust land.

**Current rule:** Where lawful public use of a state-maintained federal right-of-way removes tribal exclusion power over ordinary motorists, Montana governs the road-use claim. Subject to controlling treaties or statutes and its two exceptions, tribal adjudicatory power does not exceed corresponding substantive governing authority; applying another sovereign's law or completed exhaustion supplies no jurisdiction. The consensual-relationship exception requires a meaningful relationship between the asserted authority and dealings, contracts, leases or similar arrangements with the Tribe or members. The second exception requires conduct threatening or directly affecting tribal political integrity, economic security, health or welfare.

The same source-and-exception inquiry governs a nonmember occupancy tax on guest transactions at a nonmember hotel on non-Indian fee land. General services and a federal trader license do not establish the requisite tribal relationship; actual business dealings must meaningfully connect to the levy. Ordinary revenue needs, services and business presence alone do not establish the second exception. No express tax-consent or privity requirement governs every case.

Montana also governs state officers executing process on retained trust land to investigate an off-reservation offense. Title matters but does not alone supply authority. Use of tribal warrants in that sovereign cooperation does not itself establish the qualifying first-exception regulatory undertaking, and individual injury alone does not establish the second exception for that enforcement category. Superior federal authority, express cooperative contracts and unrelated private conduct present different sources or settings. Once judicial review establishes the absence of authority, further tribal litigation of personal defenses is not required; authority and personal immunity remain distinct.

**Authority by component:**

- Strate v. A-1 Contractors — I. This authorized public highway falls within Montana's nonmember framework, 1997-04-28; Scalia, all nine
- Strate v. A-1 Contractors — II. A tribal forum requires an adequate source of governing power, 1997-04-28; eight Associates
- Strate v. A-1 Contractors — III. The subcontract does not bring this ordinary highway claim within the consensual exception, 1997-04-28; all nine
- Strate v. A-1 Contractors — IV. The supported interests do not satisfy the self-government exception, 1997-04-28; all nine

- Fee-land tax and distinct exceptions: Canonical Decision Record `Atkinson_Trading_Co_v_Shirley_merits_2001-05-29.md`, Public Projection / Holdings / 1. Tribal tax power over these nonmember fee-land transactions requires an applicable source or exception, 2001-05-29; Stone-Zsela's unanimous opinion.
- Retained-land starting framework: Canonical Decision Record `Nevada_v_Hicks_merits_2001-06-25.md`, Public Projection / Holdings / I. Retained trust land does not eliminate the nonmember authority inquiry, 2001-06-25; all nine Justices.
- State-enforcement tort authority and no further defense litigation: Canonical Decision Record `Nevada_v_Hicks_merits_2001-06-25.md`, Public Projection / Holdings / II. These state-enforcement searches do not establish tribal tort authority; IV. No further tribal litigation of these rejected claims is required, and federal relief remains bounded, 2001-06-25; Scalia with Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Ginsburg.

**Present operation effective:** Strate, April 28, 1997 for highway claims; Atkinson, May 29, 2001 for fee-land taxation; Hicks, June 25, 2001 for the specified state-enforcement claims.

**Exceptions and limits:** Authorized public use does not convey fee title or extinguish all compatible tribal authority. A commercial contract does not submit its party to every reservation claim; no universal privity or third-party-tort bar is adopted. Absence of jurisdiction does not itself establish immunity, proper parties or every equitable predicate for a federal injunction, and creates no refund action. These defined settings establish no controlling all-land Montana rule or general rule for every private nonmember activity on retained land. Taxes on members, qualifying leases and independently authorized activity remain distinct. The tax decision leaves open whether sufficient operator contacts could ever support a tax whose incidence is on guests. Neither state employment nor personal-capacity pleading independently answers all claims. Search legality, personal immunity, causation and damages require their own adjudication.

**Holdings navigation:** Strate v. A-1 Contractors (1997-04-28) — This authorized public highway falls within Montana's nonmember framework; Strate v. A-1 Contractors (1997-04-28) — A tribal forum requires an adequate source of governing power; Strate v. A-1 Contractors (1997-04-28) — The subcontract does not bring this ordinary highway claim within the consensual exception; Strate v. A-1 Contractors (1997-04-28) — The supported interests do not satisfy the self-government exception. [Atkinson Trading Co. v. Shirley, 532 U.S. 645 — Tribal taxation of nonmember fee-land transactions](HOLDINGS.md#atkinson-trading-co-v-shirley-532-us-645); [Nevada v. Hicks — Tribal tort authority over state enforcement searches](HOLDINGS.md#nevada-v-hicks-1).

## Standards and Tests selection: Coal reservations and distinct coalbed methane

### Coal reservations and distinct coalbed methane

**Governing question:** Whether the 1909 and 1910 Coal Lands Acts’ coal reservations include chemically distinct methane.

**Current rule:** Those coal reservations do not include naturally occurring, chemically distinct methane held by physical adsorption in coal or in its fractures merely because the gas is associated with the reservoir. Coal and its expressly accompanying rights remain reserved. Increased profitability of extracting a distinct substance does not change the resource Congress named, while new valuable uses of coal do not remove coal from the reservation. The later transfer of the retained coal estate in trust does not enlarge it.

**Authority by component:**

- Amoco Production Co. v. Southern Ute Indian Tribe — Canonical Decision Record, Holdings, “The reservation of coal does not include this distinct methane gas”, 1999-06-07; Stevens’s eight-Justice Opinion of the Court.

**Present operation effective:** Amoco, June 7, 1999.

**Exceptions and limits:** The construction establishes no gas-access code, destruction right or general rule for all minerals or later-developed uses. Other gas reservations, migrated gas, allocation, surface access, injury to coal, compensation and remaining trust questions remain governed separately.

**Holdings navigation:** [Amoco Production Co. v. Southern Ute Indian Tribe — The reservation of coal does not include this distinct methane gas](HOLDINGS.md#the-reservation-of-coal-does-not-include-this-distinct-methane-gas-1).

## Standing State selection: 1. Current Court

## 1. Current Court

All nine seats are occupied at the opening of OT2003. The Supreme Court Composition register controls the roster, service dates and seniority. All nine Justices are seated before OT2003 opens, subject to established case-specific nonparticipation; no vacancy or new oath-date participation condition applies.

| Seniority | Justice | Office | Seat | Supreme Court service began | Current office began | Source and effective date |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Alex-Lamar Stone-Zsela | Chief Justice | Chief Justice line | October 7, 1991 | October 7, 1991 | Composition register; opening substitution effective October 7, 1991. |
| 2 | John Paul Stevens | Senior Associate Justice | Stevens line | December 19, 1975 | December 19, 1975 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 3 | Sandra Day O'Connor | Associate Justice | O'Connor line | September 25, 1981 | September 25, 1981 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 4 | Antonin Scalia | Associate Justice | Scalia line | September 26, 1986 | September 26, 1986 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 5 | Anthony M. Kennedy | Associate Justice | Kennedy line | February 18, 1988 | February 18, 1988 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 6 | David H. Souter | Associate Justice | Souter line | October 9, 1990 | October 9, 1990 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 7 | Clarence Thomas | Associate Justice | Marshall line | October 23, 1991 | October 23, 1991 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 8 | Ruth Bader Ginsburg | Associate Justice | White line | August 10, 1993 | August 10, 1993 | Composition register; seated at the OT2003 opening. |
| 9 | Stephen G. Breyer | Most-junior Associate Justice | Blackmun line | August 3, 1994 | August 3, 1994 | Composition register; took seat August 3, 1994. |

**Opinion-assignment seniority:** For each judgment component, the Chief Justice assigns when he is in the judgment majority. Otherwise the most senior participating Associate Justice in that majority assigns, in this order: Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer.
